R. Q. 1 بَقْبَقَ الكُوزُ , (S, M,) بِالمَآءِ, (M,) [inf. n. بَقْبَقَةٌ, q. v. infrà,] The mug made a [guggling or gurgling] sound with the water [on being dipped into it or on one's pouring out from it]. (S, * M.) And بَقْبَقَتِ القِدْرُ The cooking-pot boiled [so as to make a sound of bubbling]. (M.) ―
-b2- See also 1. ―
-b3- بَقْبَقَ عَلَيْنَا الكَلَامَ i. q. فَرَّقَهُ [lit. He scattered speech (app. meaning he jabbered) at us, or against us: compare بَقَّ عَلَى القَوْمِ, or بَقَّ كَلَامَهُ, above]. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
